findings.title: Extracted module silently changes template_actions guard semantics (empty templateSetKey now blocks instead of passing)
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md § Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'Separate code state, proof state, and canon/doc state. Do not collapse them.' The commit is framed as a pure extraction refactor, but the template_actions guard logic changed: old code `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey)` would skip the linked check when templateSetKey is empty (returning true); new code `if (templateActions.length) { if (!tsk) return false; }` now returns false in that case. This is a behavioral change, not a neutral extraction, and it is not disclosed in the commit message or PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) confirm the new stricter behavior is intentional and document it as a bug-fix in PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md per the Document Authority Model, or (b) restore the original semantics in the pure function to make this a true neutral extraction, then add a separate commit for the intentional fix.
evidence: CLAUDE.md § Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'If docs and code disagree, say so explicitly.' and 'Do not infer closure from green local behavior alone.'
CLAUDE.md § Document Authority Model: 'PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md — reality/failure/proof log' — behavioral changes must be logged.
Old workbench.js (HEAD~1): 'if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey) { ... }' — empty templateSetKey bypasses the linked check, returns true.
New workbench-template-gating.js line 52-56: 'if (templateActions.length) { if (!tsk) return false; ... }' — empty templateSetKey with non-empty template_actions now returns false.
git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- web/workbench.js confirms the logic substitution without any comment noting the semantic change.

findings.title: Commit discipline: two dirty files present at commit time were correctly excluded, but no prior checkpoint commit isolates them
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md § Commit Discipline (MANDATORY): 'If unrelated files are dirty, stage and commit only the intended slice. Do not use unrelated dirt as a reason to skip the checkpoint commit.' The intended slice was committed correctly. However, src/pipeline_v2/service.py and tests/test_template_registry_schema.py remain dirty without a prior checkpoint commit covering them, indicating those changes have accumulated without their own checkpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit or stash src/pipeline_v2/service.py and tests/test_template_registry_schema.py in their own checkpoint slice before continuing.
evidence: CLAUDE.md § Commit Discipline: 'Do not let multiple implementation chunks stack up uncommitted.' and 'If commit discipline is missed, treat that as a process failure and correct it immediately.'
git status output: 'M src/pipeline_v2/service.py' and 'M tests/test_template_registry_schema.py' — both modified and uncommitted at time of review.

residual_risks: The semantic change to template_actions guard (empty templateSetKey now returns false) may silently regress live workbench behavior for any template-set where templateSetKey is not yet populated; no Playwright acceptance test covers this path.

The commit claims to close a Step 11 canonical spec item, but the canonical spec doc (docs/plans/2026-03-23-workbench-canonical-spec.md §11) has not been verified as updated to reflect WIRED/PARTIAL status — risk of stale canon.

workbench-template-gating.js is loaded via absolute path '/workbench-template-gating.js' in workbench.html — correct for root-hosted deployment, but this assumption is not flagged anywhere; base-path hosting would require the same path prefix handling applied to workbench.js.
testing_gaps: No test covers the exact old behavior of empty-templateSetKey + non-empty template_actions returning true; if the semantic change is unintentional, the new tests will mask the regression rather than catch it.

The test harness uses JSON.stringify for deep equality which cannot distinguish object key insertion order on all Node versions; canonical ordering tests for getEnabledActions may be unreliable on Node < 12.

No integration or Playwright test verifies that workbench.html loads workbench-template-gating.js before workbench.js and that window.__workbenchTemplateGating is populated at the point workbench.js destructures it.
